To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) The presence of CP- AMPARs does not confer instability onto synapses that have undergone experience-dependent potentiation in mouse somatosensory neocortex.
(1) The presence of CP-AMPA receptors does not confer synaptic instability onto recently potentiate synapses in mouse somatosensory barrel cortex.

1) the presence of CP AMPARs in the postsynaptic density is not required for synaptic depression after potentiation in somatosensy cortex, and 2) CP AMPARs may be present in the postsynpatic density in control animals, but do not lead to synaptic depression in the absence of NMDAR activation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms underlying experience-dependent plasticity in primary somatosensary cortex.
how the brain processes sensory information, and the mechanisms that underlie learning.
understanding the role of calcium-permeability in the regulation of synaptic strength in cortical circuits.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of calcium permeable AMPAR (CP-AMPARS) is neither a necessary nor a sufficient cause for the synaptic depression that occurs after potentiation in somatosensary cortex.
the presence of Ca(2+)-permeable AMPAR does not necessarily imply that these synapses are labile.
the presence of calcium-permeating AMPARs is not sufficient for the induction or maintenance of experience-induced plasticity, but may be required for its expression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that CP-AMPA receptors are neither sufficient nor essential for the expression of plasticity at synapses in the barrel cortex.
the presence of Ca-permeable AMPA receptors (CP- AMPARs) is not necessary for the depression of potentiated synapses after single-whisker experience in vivo.
CP-AMPs are neither necessary nor sufficient for the expression of plasticity, and are not necessary for the expression of lability after plasticity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of calcium-permeability in AMPA receptors is not sufficient for the synaptic lability observed after experience-dependent potentiation.
the presence of calcium-permeability is neither sufficient nor necessary to cause synaptic lability after experience-induced plasticity.
the presence of Ca2+-permeable AMPAR (CP-AMPAs) is not sufficient to induce synaptic depression.
